_comment: Falsifying inputs written BY HAND after reading a mutant's diff, for (mutant, rule) pairs where the Lean proof is lost and no arm supplied a usable input. harness/confirm.py replays them like any other. Each entry says why it was needed.

why.cm-l14: `i *= 1` in Ledger::total: the loop never advances. Proptest (edge) reports these two rules only as a hang, which has no shrunk input; Kani fails them on an unwinding assertion whose concrete ledger does NOT falsify the rule (the loop keeps adding a non-zero first balance until the sum overflows and returns None, which is the right answer). A ledger whose FIRST balance is 0 loops forever.
why.cm-l34: `i *= 1` in Ledger::apply_batch: the counter stays 0, so the first transfer is applied again and again until it stops being valid. A zero-amount transfer between two existing accounts stays valid for ever, so the call never returns. Rows and proptest (edge) report these rules only as hangs, which have no shrunk input; Kani fails them on an unwinding assertion (or times out), and the inputs it reports need not loop for ever. The inputs below do, by reading the diff.
